claims.text: The untreated eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical dual-phase lamellar colony structure.
The untreated alloy exhibits localized dislocation pile-ups at internal phase boundaries.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal lamellar boundaries produce stress concentrations, limited tensile ductility, brittleness, and premature failure at room temperature.
The untreated alloy has high strength.
The proposed intervention is 5–10 annealing cycles between 500°C and 700°C, each including a 30-minute high-temperature hold followed by rapid cooling.
Repeated thermal cycling promotes diffusion and redistribution of constituent elements to phase boundaries.
The treatment produces graded interphase boundaries containing enriched solute layers.
Solute-enriched graded interfaces have modified chemistry and stronger bonding.
The graded interfaces have enhanced toughness.
The modified interfaces mediate plastic strain and disrupt or alleviate dislocation pile-ups.
Tougher graded interfaces redistribute local stresses and reduce stress concentrations.
Reduced dislocation pile-ups and stress concentrations minimize microcracking and delay crack initiation.
The treatment is expected to increase room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
The treatment is expected to improve resistance to microcrack initiation relative to the untreated alloy.
The treatment is expected to maintain or potentially increase yield and ultimate tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed treatment is applicable to specimens subsequently tested under standard room-temperature tensile-loading conditions.
Overly aggressive segregation may form brittle intermetallic phases.
The effectiveness of the treatment depends on precise control of the thermal cycles and segregation level.
